newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran president cleared of corruption charges.
newsitem.headline: Honduran president cleared of corruption charges.

text.p: Honduran President Carlos Roberto Reina was cleared of corruption charges on Tuesday when a criminal court closed its investigation of him, a court spokesman said.
Reina was elected in November 1993 after campaigning hard against corruption, so the court's announcement of its probe last week sent shock waves through this Central American country.
The case stemmed from a $242,000 payment Reina's government made to workers of the U.S.-owned Tela Railroad Co. to settle a strike in 1994.
The government took the unusual step of paying the workers, arguing that it was cheaper than letting the strike continue.

"The ... court closed the investigation of the complaint of misappropriation of funds and abuse of power against President Carlos Roberto Reina," a court spokesman told Reuters, requesting anonymity. "The investigation was closed because no legal culpability was found."
Also cleared on Tuesday were two of Reina's Cabinet ministers.
A complaint against them was filed by an opposition legislator who sought to repeal the executive immunity enjoyed by Reina and his Cabinet and bring them to trial.
